refnamediv.refpurpose: Compute the partial fraction expansion (PFE) of a digital filter.

refsynopsisdiv.title: Syntax
refsynopsisdiv.synopsis: [r, p, f, m] = residuez(B, A) [r, p, f, m] = residuez(B, A, tol)

listitem.para: Numerator coefficients of the digital filter (vector).
Denominator coefficients of the digital filter (vector).
(optional) Tolerance for pole-zero matching. Ignored in this implementation.
Column vector containing the residues of the filter poles.
Column vector containing the poles of the filter.
Row vector containing the FIR part of the filter, if any. Empty if no FIR part exists.
Column vector containing the multiplicities of the poles.

refsection.title: Description
refsection.para: The `residuez` function computes the partial fraction expansion of a digital filter represented by the transfer function: H(z) = B(z) / A(z) where `B` and `A` are the numerator and denominator coefficients, respectively.
The function separates the filter into two parts: 1. The FIR part `f`, which represents the feedforward portion of the filter. 2. The IIR part, represented by the residues `r` and poles `p`.

If the numerator degree is less than the denominator degree (`nb < na`), the FIR part `f` is empty, and the filter is represented as: H(z) = r(1) / [1 - p(1)/z]^m(1) + ... + r(N) / [1 - p(N)/z]^m(N) where `N` is the number of poles.

If the numerator degree is greater than or equal to the denominator degree (`nb >= na`), the FIR part `f` is non-empty, and the filter is represented as: H(z) = f(1) + f(2)/z + f(3)/z^2 + ... + f(M+1)/z^M + R(z) where `R(z)` is the parallel one-pole filter bank.
Notes - The polynomials `B` and `A` must have real coefficients. - The function uses MATLAB's `residue` function internally to compute the residues and poles.

refsection.title: Examples
refsection.programlisting: // Compute the partial fraction expansion of a filter: B = [1, 1, 1] A = [1, -2, 1] [r, p, f, m] = residuez(B, A)
